Hey guys, how was your summer break?

For those of you who haven't seen, while @vegard is still officially head mod of the subreddit, he is in the process of handing over full control to me. A CSS theme for the subreddit is in the works over at /v/F1Test, and if any of you are programatically inclined please do message me if you feel you could help. The plans for the immediate future are to try and run a smoother and more coherent selection of Race Threads for the coming races.

 

With those formalities out of the way, I propose that we end the 3 weeks of summer with 3 weeks of great racing!

Week 1: 21st - 23rd August

As you all know, the Belgian Grand Prix is on this weekend, and hopefully we are gonna see some changes in position around the field as the teams have been working over the summer break. It also brings us the first use of the new starting procedure, where drivers have reduced assistance in setting the clutch bite point; hopefully this is going to lead to a great start and some changing of positions before the cars stream off into the Ardennes Forest.

Week 2: 28th - 30th August

Luckily there is a choice here for everyone, as there is a WEC and an IndyCar race running.

WEC are holding the 6 hours of Nurburgring, which is sure to be a great race and is the first round post - Le Mans. For those of you iffy about comitting 6 hours, you really don't have to. Just leave a screen with it on and you will find yourself following the race at your own pace. You shoud really consider giving it a watch or risk missing out on great racing like what happened at Silverstone earlier in the year.

As for Indycar, this weekend they will be holding the last race of the season at Sonoma, where our boy Montoya has a chance of winning the championship. Currently he is 9 points ahed of his closest competitor, Graham Rahal, so things are about to get stressful.

Luckily because of the timings you can watch both live, with an hour gap from the end of the WEC and the start of Indycar race. Please head over to /v/WEC and /v/IndyCar and show them some love.

Week 3: 4th - 6th September

What better way to bring in September than with Monza. The F1 circus is heading over there where hopefully we will see Ferrari bring their A-Game and give the Mercs a real challenge. Monza is the fastest track on the calendar, and we are gonna get to see all the cars fit skinny little front and rear wings with tightened up bodywork. This festival of speed is a great way to round out our 3 weeks of racing.

If you've read all this, well done, and thanks for sticking to the end. I hope you enjoy the next 3 weeks, but as this sub is in its infancy, it would be really helpful if you could message us any suggestions or ideas via the modmail. Thanks for all the great posts keeping our F1 scratches itched over the summer!

I'm going to go against what others have said and say "yes", but the sweating is a side effect.

As others have correctly mentioned, sweating is one of the body's mechanisms for releasing heat. But, let's talk about how the heat is generated...

The body takes in fuel in the form of macronutrients (carbohydrates, lipids and protein) and breaks these down for energy so that it can do things/survive. Excess fuel tends to get stored as fat (white adipose tissue; WAT). The actual biochemical pathways involved are complex (I could spend a week walking you through glycolysis, cellular respiration, etc. and we'd still have only scratched the surface); suffice it to say, the body only uses fuel when it is doing work.

There is, however, a short circuit called 'uncoupling'; you could think of this as uncoupling the need to do work from the ability to burn fuel. This is what DNP does for everyone brave/stupid enough to use it. The thing is, the body also has a natural mechanism of uncoupling: thermogenin in brown adipose tissue (BAT). BAT is a special type of fat tissue that evolution has given us, which enables us to survive in cold climates. When uncoupling occurs, the energy produced form burning the fuel has to go somewhere; it's not going into work, so it is lost as heat (again, we could spend a long time going through the quantum chemistry and thermodynamics of this, but it's not necessary unless you want to understand the intricacies of the process).

So, getting back to your question, I'm suspicious that you may have a larger than usual amount of BAT (or excessive noradrenalin, or a mutation somewhere in the signalling pathway that causes hyperactivity, etc.), consequently, your body may be consuming more fuel than normal, producing more heat than normal, and sweating more in order to dissipate that heat. I'm certain your GP could refer you to the relevant specialist if you wanted to test this theory; personally, though, I'd just count it as a blessing.
